title: Isandro and the Verdict
premise: When the coffin of Harrow's Gap founder Elias Verne is exhumed for a centennial reburial and found empty, retired detective August Yarrow realizes the empty coffin mirrors a gap in the town's own ledger—a coded account book he's kept hidden in his bookshop for twelve years. As August deciphers the ledger, he uncovers that Verne never died in 1912; he fled with the town's founding fortune, and a line of respected families has been maintaining the lie ever since. The current mayor, Diana Verne-Cole, is killing to keep the secret, and August's own missing memories of the night his partner died are the final key. In the end, August publishes the decoded ledger, accepts that his partner's death was his own doing, and chooses to stay in Harrow's Gap—visible at last.
about_author: Felix Reyes is a former small-town newspaper archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obituaries before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about the secrets towns keep and the people paid to keep them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Alphabetical Order
chapters.summary: August Yarrow's POV. In his failing bookshop, August catalogs a donation of old town records, hiding one slim ledger among the poetry. Establish his routines, his tremor, and the twelve-year silence since his partner's death. Emotional beat: the comfort and prison of order.

chapters.title: An Invitation in Good Handwriting
chapters.summary: August's POV. Mayor Diana Verne-Cole personally invites him to the centennial exhumation of Elias Verne, watching him too closely for comfort. He notices she uses a phrase only the old founding families know. Emotional beat: unease beneath civility.

chapters.title: Dirt, Brass, and Nothing at All
chapters.summary: August's POV, with a brief interlude from gravedigger Tomás Ruiz. The coffin is opened before the whole town: inside, only a ledger-shaped indentation and a century-old brass key. Tomás sees August go pale. Emotional beat: public shock masking private recognition.

chapters.title: The Book That Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: August's POV. That night he compares the coffin's dimensions to the hidden ledger in his shop—it fits perfectly. Flashback fragment: the night his partner Ruth died, a fire, a scream he can't place. Emotional beat: dread that his past is the present's blueprint.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Polite Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: August and Ruth's daughter, Nadia, now a journalist, arriving unannounced. She wants a story on the empty coffin; he wants her gone before she digs into her mother's file. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into distance.

chapters.title: The Verne-Cole Family Album
chapters.summary: August's POV. He visits the historical society and finds photos where Elias Verne's face has been scraped out of a 1913 group portrait—recently, by a blade, not time. Emotional beat: the past is being edited by living hands.

chapters.title: What Tomás Dug Up Besides Bones
chapters.summary: Tomás Ruiz's POV. Tomás confesses to August that he found a second, older coffin fragment beneath Verne's—containing actual remains—and was paid by the mayor's office to keep quiet. Emotional beat: guilt looking for an ally.

chapters.title: The Ledger's First Entry
chapters.summary: August's POV. He begins decoding the ledger: it's a double-entry book of debts and favors running from 1912 to the present day, written in a cipher based on Verne's published sermons. The last entry is dated the night Ruth died. Emotional beat: the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Nadia's Questions, August's Evasions
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia interviews townsfolk and senses August knows more; she finds Ruth's old case file missing its final page. August lies to her face and hates himself for it. Emotional beat: love expressed as obstruction.

chapters.title: A Fire in the Poetry Section
chapters.summary: August's POV. Someone torches the back of the bookshop; the ledger survives only because August moved it that morning on a hunch. The arsonist wore a mayoral staff lanyard. Emotional beat: his sanctuary is no longer safe.

chapters.title: The Sermons of Elias Verne
chapters.summary: August's POV. Deep in the cipher, August discovers Verne didn't flee with the money—he was smuggled out by the founding families after he tried to return the stolen fortune, and the town's prosperity was built on his silence. Emotional beat: the founder as victim, not villain.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Mayor
chapters.summary: August's POV. Diana hosts him for a tense dinner, offering him the historical society directorship—hush money in a nicer shape. She quotes the ledger's phrasing, revealing she knows it exists. Emotional beat: corruption wearing its best face.

chapters.title: Tomás Stops Coming to Work
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Tomás disappears; his truck is found at the quarry. Nadia and August, now uneasy allies, realize the mayor's office is eliminating witnesses. Emotional beat: fear converting rivalry into partnership.

chapters.title: The Page Ruth Tore Out
chapters.summary: August's POV. August finally recalls the missing case-file page: Ruth had decoded part of the ledger twelve years ago and confronted him with it. His memory of that night is a locked room he built himself. Emotional beat: memory as self-protection and self-betrayal.

chapters.title: Quarry Water
chapters.summary: August's POV. Divers find Tomás's body staged as an accident, but his hands clutch a scrap of ledger paper—proof he'd been reading it. August realizes Tomás died because August taught him the cipher's existence. Emotional beat: guilt compounding into resolve.

chapters.title: The Founding Families' Meeting
chapters.summary: August's POV, eavesdropping. August sneaks into the historical society and witnesses Diana and the surviving old families vote to 'close the account'—destroy the ledger and its keepers, as they did in 1912 and again twelve years ago. Emotional beat: power as a standing appointment.

chapters.title: What August Did That Night
chapters.summary: August's POV, full flashback. The memory unlocks: twelve years ago Ruth gave August the ledger to hide, and when the fire started, August fled with the ledger and left her inside, believing her already dead—a choice he's buried under twelve years of alphabetized silence. Emotional beat: devastating self-reckoning.

chapters.title: Confession at the Bookshop Counter
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. August tells Nadia everything—her mother's death, his cowardice, the ledger. Instead of condemnation, she asks for his help finishing what Ruth started. Emotional beat: forgiveness neither of them feels entitled to.

chapters.title: The Centennial Address
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the centennial gala, Diana announces the 'reburial' of an empty coffin with a new legend. August slips backstage to swap the ceremonial coffin's contents with the decoded ledger, printed in full. Emotional beat: quiet courage before the storm.

chapters.title: Closing the Account
chapters.summary: August's POV, climax. Diana catches him; a confrontation in the society archive turns violent as she tries to burn the ledger and him with it. Nadia arrives with the sheriff—she'd tipped him off. Tomás's evidence and the printed copies make destruction pointless. Diana is arrested. Emotional beat: the fire finally faced, not fled.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: August's POV. Elias Verne's true remains are laid to rest with his name restored; Ruth's case is reopened and closed honestly. August gives Nadia the original ledger for the public record. Emotional beat: grief given a grave at last.

chapters.title: Shelved Under Y
chapters.summary: August's POV, coda. The bookshop reopens with new windows and a shelf of local history—including the ledger's story. A customer asks the quiet shopkeeper who he is; August answers with his whole name. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed, invisibility voluntarily ended.
